## Purpose

This section covers the controlled route from authorised BNR source data to approved analytical products and the public Info-Hub.

CVD event metrics, tabulations and routine CVD briefings share one CVD preparation layer. CVD mortality has its own six-step workflow because it starts from the death-certificate source and includes a separate mortality classification stage.

For exact paths, files and commands, use the [Technical Manual analytical workflows](../../technical/workflows/overview.qmd).

## The tools and their jobs

| Tool | Operational role |
|---|---|
| **REDCap** | Holds the authoritative current CVD event records and mortality death-certificate records used by the two analytical routes. |
| **Stata** | Extracts, prepares and analyses data; creates review packages; records approval; promotes approved analytical products. |
| **VS Code** | Edits Quarto narrative and website source and shows the Git changes proposed for publication. |
| **Quarto** | Renders the approved website presentation and downloads catalogue. |
| **GitHub** | Records reviewed public changes and deploys the static Info-Hub. |

## CVD shared preparation plus mortality

CVD events Steps 1–3, accessed in Stata through **User > BNR > Update CVD dashboard**, form the common CVD analytical preparation layer. Step 3 creates the private deidentified inputs used by the three CVD downstream pathways.

Mortality begins separately under **User > BNR > Update mortality dashboard** and runs through its own Steps 1–6.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    A["Authorised CVD REDCap release"] --> B["Stata: CVD events Steps 1–3"]
    B --> C["CVD event metrics Steps 4–6"]
    B --> D["Tabulation Steps 1–3"]
    B --> E["Briefing Steps 1–3"]

    M["Authorised mortality death-certificate release"] --> N["Mortality Steps 1–6"]

    C --> F["Approved public products"]
    D --> F
    E --> F
    N --> F
    F --> G["VS Code + Quarto + GitHub"]
```

## Rules common to every pathway

1. Use the same release identity throughout one controlled workflow.
2. Keep source data, logs, staging packages and review files in the private workspace.
3. Inspect quality, method, plausibility and disclosure risk before approval.
4. Approve the exact reviewed package through the relevant Stata step.
5. Use the controlled Stata publication step; do not copy individual analytical output files by hand.
6. Update Quarto content only from approved public products or their website mirrors.
7. Render and inspect the site before committing and pushing public changes.

Stop when the source period, package identity, result, disclosure status or approval is unclear. Correct the authoritative source record or version-controlled code, then rerun from the earliest affected stage.
